Decentralized peer sampling

Shared membership traces and sampling demand, local protocol state, counted message delivery. Select a scenario to compare sampling quality, availability, and communication cost.

Reading the results. Total variation (TV) ranges from 0 to 1; lower is better. Uniformity is conditional on returning a live, non-self peer. Always read it alongside live-sample rate. “Local excess” subtracts a matched ideal IID sampler's local TV; finite sampling noise can make it slightly negative. Small samples produce high empirical TV even for ideal samplers.

Table values are means across seeds; ± values are approximate normal 95% confidence half-widths (absent for one seed). Curves average matching observation times. Sampling outcomes are grouped by request window, including later replies. Traffic is cumulative since warmup; final table costs include the drain of outstanding messages. Bytes use compact JSON payloads plus a configurable header, not measured TCP/IP traffic.

BASALT's hierarchical mode targets an IP-prefix distribution, so nonzero TV against uniform identities is expected. Its intended-distribution local TV is available in the CSV/JSON. PeerSwap assumes no failures in its paper model; join attachment and timeout cleanup here are experimental extensions. These runs do not evaluate Byzantine resistance.
